story.head: The Stars’ power play has a target
paras: The Blue Jackets (5-6-0) lost 3-2 to Carolina on Thursday, and the Stars (7-5-1) lost 5-2 to Montréal the same night. Going in, the Jackets are seventh in the Metropolitan (tied for 28th in the NHL) and the Stars fourth in the Central (tied for 16th).

The Blue Jackets get their defensemen shooting (5th) and get a lot of their shots blocked (29th). They also have a leaky penalty kill (29th), so the Stars’ power play (2nd) could do real damage when they’re shorthanded. Columbus has scored 2.45 goals a game, the fourth fewest in the league. On the other side, the Stars block more shots than anyone (1st) and play slow, tight games (lowest), but take more penalties than they draw (31st). Dallas has allowed 2.23 goals a game, the fewest in the league. The Stars get in close, but the Blue Jackets mostly shoot from distance.

Kent Johnson (7 G / 4 A / 11 P in 11 GP) leads the Blue Jackets in scoring, and Charlie Coyle (1 G / 8 A / 9 P in 11 GP) is next in line. For the Stars, Mikko Rantanen (6 G / 10 A / 16 P in 13 GP) leads the way in scoring, with eight points in his last five games. Jason Robertson (5 G / 8 A / 13 P in 13 GP) isn’t far behind.
Cam Talbot (3-2-0 / .893 SV% in 5 GS) is in line to start for Columbus. Jake Oettinger (6-3-1 / .917 SV% in 10 GS) has been a rock in net for Dallas and will likely start.
